title: Switching Martial Arts Software: Data & Card Migration
description: Switching martial arts software? What 11 vendors move for free (students, ranks, attendance, saved cards), timelines and how to keep autopay running.
h1: Switching martial arts software: what moves, what doesn't
body:
Most school owners who switch martial arts software aren't worried about the new features. They're worried about three things: losing student records, losing belt and attendance history, and families' autopay breaking during the move. This guide compares what 11 vendors say they will move for you, what they won't, and how to plan the cutover so billing keeps running.

We checked each vendor's own pricing, switching and help pages on November 22, 2026. We haven't migrated a school ourselves and we don't publish ratings. Where a vendor doesn't say, we write "not stated" or unknown.

Why saved cards are the hard part

Your school software usually doesn't hold families' card numbers. The payment processor does. So whether autopay survives a switch depends on whether your old processor will hand the card data to the new one, not just on the software companies.

  • Moving cards between processors is a formal process. Stripe says it only transfers card data to another PCI DSS Level 1 processor, and that its export doesn't include payment history or subscriptions. Cards saved through Stripe's Link are excluded. (Stripe: request a payment data export)
  • It can take a while. Moving cards into Stripe, Stripe says processors can take anywhere from a few days to several months to produce the export, and some charge a fee. Once Stripe has valid data, imports typically finish within 10 business days. Security codes (CVC) are never transferred. (Stripe: import payment data)
  • Some vendors skip card transfer. Kicksite doesn't import card or bank details. It says some software charges the school a significant fee to export encrypted card data, and that the cardholder is often a parent rather than the student. Instead it sends bulk payment-method invitations so families re-enter cards through a secure link. (Kicksite import list)
  • Others say members won't notice. Zen Planner says saved card and ACH details migrate so members don't re-enter anything. Gymdesk says it helps transfer saved cards, with timing set by your current processor. MAAT says it migrates cards and SEPA/BACS mandates. Martialytics says it adopts live Stripe and GoCardless subscriptions in place.

If families do have to re-enter cards, expect a few to drop off. Martialytics' own buying guide warns that some members won't re-enter card details. Plan reminders, and keep the old system billing until the new one is collecting. Processing rates also change when you switch; compare them on martial arts billing software and payment processing fees explained.

Belt ranks and attendance history

Belt and attendance history are where martial arts migrations differ from gym migrations. Kicksite imports a student's current program and rank (the names must match ranks you've already set up in Kicksite) but not promotion history or attendance history. Zen Planner says attendance history moves over and tells schools to confirm belt and rank fields with their implementation specialist before migrating. Martialytics' CSV wizard imports ranks. Before you start, set up your programs and rank lists in the new system so imported ranks have something to match.

Kicksite's switch page suggests checking whether your current software needs advance notice to cancel, and how long you keep access afterwards. Recess runs its migration while your old system stays live. In short, don't cancel until the new system has your data.

A switching plan that keeps tuition coming in

  1. Read your contract. Find your renewal date and notice period (Spark, for example, asks for 30 days' notice before auto-renewal).
  2. Export everything yourself first. Spark's terms, for example, give you only a 30-day window after the contract ends to request your data. Active and inactive students, guardians, attendance, rank and promotion history, payment history and signed waivers. Keep the files even if the new vendor won't import some of them.
  3. Ask both processors about cards. Ask the new vendor exactly how saved cards and ACH move, how long it takes and who pays any export fee. Get the answer in writing.
  4. Set up programs, ranks and memberships in the new system before the import, and leave out memberships you no longer sell (Kicksite can filter old ones out if you list them).
  5. Run both systems for one billing cycle. Free trials help here: Kicksite's first 30 days are free; Gymdesk, Martialytics and MatGoat offer 30-day trials with no card; Dojo Champ gives 30 days with a card; Spark gives 8 weeks; MAAT 7 days. Recess and MatPilot have free plans.
  6. Tell families before anything changes. Zen Planner says it provides announcement templates. Kicksite sends portal and payment-method invites in bulk.
  7. Switch billing, check the first run, then cancel the old system.

Our software buying checklist covers the questions to ask during demos. If you're leaving a specific vendor, see Kicksite alternatives or Zen Planner alternatives. To keep costs down while you overlap, see free martial arts software.

faq: Can I switch martial arts software without families re-entering their cards?

Sometimes. Zen Planner says saved card and ACH details migrate so members don't re-enter them (zenplanner.com/switch), Gymdesk says it helps transfer saved cards once your current processor releases them, MAAT says it migrates cards and SEPA/BACS mandates, and Martialytics adopts live Stripe and GoCardless subscriptions. Kicksite doesn't import card data and sends families bulk payment-method invitations instead (checked 2026-11-22).
How long does it take to move to new martial arts software?

Vendors publish different figures: Kicksite says 2 business days or less once it can access your old account, Zen Planner about one week for migration and core setup, and PushPress says most gyms go live in a few days. Moving saved cards between processors can take longer. Stripe says processors take from a few days to several months to produce the export (checked 2026-11-22).

Kicksite, Zen Planner, Spark Membership, PushPress, Dojo Champ and MAAT all describe migration as free on their own pages. Stripe notes that some processors charge a fee to export card data, and Kicksite says some software charges schools a significant fee to export encrypted card info (checked 2026-11-22).
Will my belt rank and attendance history transfer?

It depends on the vendor. Kicksite imports current program and rank but not promotion or attendance history. Zen Planner says attendance history moves and asks schools to confirm belt and rank fields with their specialist first. Martialytics' CSV import wizard brings ranks across (checked 2026-11-22).
When should I cancel my old software?

After the new system has your data and its first billing run has worked. Kicksite recommends a short period with both systems active and suggests checking your current vendor's notice period; Spark's terms, for example, require 30 days' notice before an auto-renewal (checked 2026-11-22).
